reasoning: Both sets plan all three environments in full, with ID'd requirements, Given/When/Then checks and a shared-core architecture. A is the stronger technical plan. It handles time-limit truncation explicitly (GameStep.truncated, end_segment bootstrapping). Its value and policy ladders each change exactly one thing, and it deliberately leaves out advantage normalization so it does not hide a baseline. It argues that catches cannot be skipped from relative displacement. It flags the learning-volume confound in take-turns and pool. It fully settles the significance design: one-sided permutation tests, Holm correction, a minimum p of 1/252, all fixed in advance. Spec and architecture trace cleanly, and it adds gated reference comparisons and findings write-ups. A's weaknesses: the brief keeps placeholder goals ('Merged into Goal 3') and Snake-only bets. It relaxes the user's success criterion to reaching 75% of the scripted player, and lists clearly beating it as out of scope. Its stage/step naming is overloaded. It gives no explicit build order. B is more readable and better sequenced: flat Snake, then core extraction, then the tank stage, then the arena stage. Its success criteria match the user's (must beat random and scripted bots), and it adds useful ablations and an escalation reel. But its brief still reads as a Snake-only document with Goals 6 and 7 tacked on. CORE-01 gates extraction on features that now include tank and arena requirements, which is circular. Its main must-beat significance test is admittedly unresolved and may be impossible at 5 seeds. It treats the 1,000-step time limit as terminal in a +1-per-step survival task. Its frozen ideas cite the wrong CORE IDs and keep an unresolved open question. Both sets drop reward shaping, which is one of the user's target concepts. Overall, A's content advantage outweighs B's structural edge.

strengths: Explicit truncation handling: time-limit games are bootstrapped, not treated as real ends (GameStep.truncated, end_segment)

Ladders that change one thing per step (NET: online, then replay, then target, then double; PG: REINFORCE, then baseline, then GAE critic, then PPO), with advantage normalization deliberately left out so it does not act as a hidden baseline
Statistical design fully settled: one-sided permutation tests with directions fixed in advance, Holm correction, and the 1/252 minimum p-value worked out against each threshold
Co-evolution measured with fixed yardsticks (scored against scripted opponents, cross-play table, wobble), and the learning-volume confound acknowledged
Heading-up Snake view (AD-03) fixes the ambiguity of relative moves on a full board view; table-coverage breakdown on 8x8 shows why tables stop working
Reference comparisons with Stable-Baselines3, with matched settings and gated behind the hand-written learners being evaluated first (REF-03)
Tight traceability: every spec ID mapped to components; idea Spec lines match the changelog exactly
weaknesses: Brief keeps placeholder goals and Snake-only bets
Relaxes the user's success criterion (beat the scripted baseline) to reaching 75% of it, and lists clearly beating it as out of scope
'Stage' and 'step' are overloaded across NET, PG, tank and COEV, which makes cross-references hard to follow
No explicit build order; the architecture shows only the end-state core, despite the brief's 'extract when environment 2 needs it'
Very long architecture (about 9k words); the spec's Assumptions repeat requirement content
Reward shaping, one of the user's target concepts, is excluded

strengths: Clear build sequence: flat Snake code, then CORE-01 extraction, then the tank stage, then the arena stage, with a file layout for each stage and golden-run tests that guard earlier results
Success criteria match the user's: learners must beat random and scripted bots in every game
Readable, first-person brief and ideas that use standard RL names alongside plain explanations
Useful ingredient-removal ablations, including an exploration-decay ablation, plus an escalation reel and a snapshot grid for watching co-evolution
Concrete numeric acceptance examples (TAB-02 gives 1.45; PG-07 gives (-1.22, 0, 1.22); GRID-04 gives '8 of 10')
The 11-fact Snake view keeps the table and the DQN inside the CPU budget
weaknesses: Brief is still worded for Snake only (Goal 2, success list, bets), with Goals 6 and 7 appended as one-liners
CORE-01's extraction gate names features that now contain tank and arena requirements, so it is circular
The must-beat significance design is unresolved; the docs admit a seed-level test cannot pass Holm correction with 5 seeds
No truncation flag; the 1,000-step time limit is treated as terminal in a +1-per-step survival task
The PPO rung adds clipping, multiple passes and advantage normalization at once; the confound from fewer learning steps under alternating and pool is not acknowledged
Frozen ideas cite the wrong CORE IDs and keep an unresolved open question; the architecture has history residue
No library comparison or findings write-up is planned; reward shaping is excluded
